references.text: The context that mentions the Arnon as the border between Moab and the Amorites is directly linked to the mention of the Arnon in verse 14.
Moses refers to the Arnon valley and the Lord's command to cross it, which connects to the military actions mentioned in the Book of the Wars of the Lord.
Describes the conquest of the cities along the Arnon valley, which is the same geographical area mentioned in the Book of the Wars of the Lord.
Another reference to a lost book, 'The Book of Jashar' (the Book of the Upright), showing that Israel had several historical writings outside the Bible.
Jephthah mentions the Arnon as a border in his historical review of Israel's journey, referring to the same events.
The prophecy against Moab mentions the rivers of the Arnon, the same geographical area as in the Book of the Wars of the Lord.
